headline: P0046 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 15.6% vs 3.0% expected for its patient mix; elevated in every complexity tier, including patients with 0-1 chronic conditions
rationale: 29 of 186 claims (15.6%) were billed as 99215. Given this panel's complexity, about 3.0% would be expected (risk-adjusted score 3.62; peer z of 1.55, which is modest on its own). The panel is not especially sick: 102 of 186 visits are for patients with 0-1 chronic conditions, and only 11 are for patients with 4 or more. Even so, the provider's 99215 share is about 2-6x the all-provider rate in every tier. The gap is largest at the low end: 11.8% vs 2.1% for patients with 0 conditions and 8.8% vs 3.4% for patients with 1 condition. Together these two tiers account for 10 of the 29 99215s. In the sampled low-complexity 99215s, the diagnoses are mostly single and often self-limited: abdominal pain R10.9 (C0022138, C0022185), UTI N39.0 (C0022264), rash R21 (C0022287), and URI with hypertension (C0022218). The same diagnoses appear in the comparison sample billed at 99213 (C0022187 N39.0, C0022200 R10.9). By contrast, 99215s on patients with 4 or more conditions (e.g., C0022129, C0022148) look more plausible. These are random samples and no clinical documentation was provided, so this is a pattern consistent with upcoding, not a finding.
next_steps: Request and review medical records (MDM complexity and/or total time) for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with C0022138, C0022185, C0022264, C0022287 and C0022218.

Compare documentation for 99215 vs 99213 visits with the same diagnoses (e.g., C0022264 vs C0022187 for N39.0; C0022138/C0022185 vs C0022200 for R10.9) to see whether anything documented explains the higher level.
Check whether time-based billing, prolonged services or same-day procedures support the level, and review the 2024-12-25 date of service on C0022309.
Pull all 29 99215 claims, not just the sample, to confirm the tier-level pattern and check whether it is concentrated in particular dates or patients.
